title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Jailbreak Beyond Textual Jailbreak in Hidden-State Risk Space
abstract: arXiv:2607.15218v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve as high-level planners for embodied agents, where linguistically benign instructions can become unsafe once grounded in the physical world. We study whether this physically grounded jailbreak is the same safety problem as ordinary textual jailbreak. Through hidden-state direction analysis and random-split null tests, we show that textual jailbreak (TJ) and physical jailbreak (PJ) form separable signals in LLM representations across Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B, Phi-3.5 and SmolLM2. Building on this separability, we propose PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe over full hidden states. PRISM achieves 86.2--87.7\% accuracy on SafeAgentBench with 11.7--13.7\% false-positive rates (FPRs), while same-scale LLM judges over-block safe tasks at 24.7--39.0\% FPR.   To test whether the result survives lexical-shortcut controls, we introduce an interaction-balanced revision of PhysicalJailb

translated_title: 当语言安全但行动致命：在隐藏状态风险空间中探测超越文本越狱的物理越狱
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地作为具身智能体的高层规划器，其中语言上看似良性的指令一旦在物理世界中落地，就可能变得不安全。我们研究了这种物理层面的越狱是否与普通文本越狱是相同的安全问题。通过隐藏状态方向分析和随机分裂零假设检验，我们表明在Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B、Phi-3.5和SmolLM2模型中，文本越狱（TJ）和物理越狱（PJ）在LLM表征中形成可分离的信号。基于这种可分离性，我们提出了PRISM，一种在完整隐藏状态上的单层L2正则化逻辑回归探针。PRISM在SafeAgentBench上达到了86.2%-87.7%的准确率，假阳性率（FPR）为11.7%-13.7%，而同等规模的LLM评判器在安全任务上的过度阻断假阳性率高达24.7%-39.0%。为了测试结果是否在词汇捷径控制下仍然成立，我们引入了PhysicalJailb的交互平衡修订版。
tldr: 本文通过隐藏状态风险空间分析，提出PRISM探针，证明物理越狱与文本越狱在LLM表征中可分离，并以较低假阳性率高效检测物理越狱。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes PRISM, a hidden-state probe, showing physical jailbreak is separable from textual jailbreak in LLM representations, achieving high detection accuracy with low false-positive rates.
